- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.3) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to prior high.
- If model shows sharp upward spike in forecast (e.g., +5%+ over 3–5 days), true outcome often lags or overshoots — cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is positive (e.g., > 0.2) and model is flat or slightly rising, true price often rises faster — increase forecast slope by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile — add 2–3% buffer to forecast if sentiment swings >0.3 in last 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated small negative swings (e.g., -0.1 to -0.2), model tends to underestimate — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
- Model often overestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) of 30d forecast when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive — reduce forecast by 1–3% for final 5–7 days.
